source.title: Scaling and Resizing Symmetry in Feedforward Networks

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether random initialization regime affects learning performance and training speed, using validation accuracy on MNIST rather than the versions' training-error measures and benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation accuracy across initialization regimes and resizing conditions. It does not report training classification error, so those accuracy results do not establish whether training error reached zero.
record.test_reason: The study bears on V4 through its own qualitative comparisons of learning speed across critical, ordered and chaotic initializations in six-hidden-layer tanh networks on MNIST. Validation accuracy over epochs can bear on learning speed without establishing zero training error. Untrained correlation propagation alone does not establish trainable depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate but should qualify preservation: halving data, width or batch size has little reported impact at critical initialization, while reducing data to 15,000 examples causes some accuracy deterioration. The authors present evidence for scaling in untrained correlation propagation and conjecture a resizing symmetry that could enable smaller datasets or architectures with lower training cost.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fully connected tanh networks on MNIST and compares ordered, disordered, and critical initialization regimes; reports validation accuracy rather than the claim versions' training-error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization regime, input data amount, hidden-layer width, and SGD batch size affect the reported validation-accuracy outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Critical initialization approximately preserves validation accuracy when training data, hidden width or SGD batch size is halved; accuracy deteriorates somewhat at 15,000 training examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Critical initialization makes validation performance comparatively robust to the tested reductions in data, width and batch size for this MNIST tanh network.

fits_no_version.finding: Untrained networks exhibit initialization-dependent correlations and approximate power-law correlation propagation near criticality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Critical Gaussian initialization preserves input correlations across depth in the studied untrained networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Using 25,000 rather than 50,000 examples approximately halves runtime for the same number of epochs; using 15,000 reduces runtime approximately threefold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing training data lowers elapsed training time while retaining comparatively strong validation performance at critical initialization.

record.problems: The reported outcomes are validation accuracy, not training classification error. Numerical values are presented only in figures, without textual values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments use MNIST and a simple fully connected tanh network.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted because the reported accuracy results do not measure training classification error or another outcome named by the claim versions. Figure 7–10 report validation accuracy for initialization and resizing conditions; no exact values are stated in the text.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and effects of model size or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima and extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.

Maximum trainable depth; direct gradient preservation measurements during training; comparisons across activation functions; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; orthogonal convolution kernels and 10,000-layer training. Exact learning-speed differences cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature evolution and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, higher learning-rate tolerance and Fixup.

missing.what: Qualitative learning-speed comparisons across initialization regimes under data reduction. The record declares omitted validation-accuracy results but overlooks the text's explicit learning-speed findings; these should be captured without inventing numerical values.

record.verdict_notes: No rows were supplied. The V4 verdict rests on qualitative learning-speed statements in the study text. Accuracy robustness and untrained correlation statistics do not independently demonstrate faster optimization or greater trainable depth.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects in plain or residual networks, identity shortcuts, and training without normalization.

The paper compares ordered, disordered, and critical initialization regimes and reports validation accuracy, but does not measure training speed numerically or report training error. It does not test activation-matched, orthogonal, or 10,000-layer initialization claims.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no normalization and learning-rate tolerance.

relationships.condition: Six-hidden-layer tanh networks trained with SGD on MNIST, especially after reducing training data to 25,000 or 15,000 examples.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 5.1 text, with no extracted row ids: critical initialization preserves the validation learning trajectory at 25,000 examples, whereas ordered initialization loses accuracy and learning speed; at 15,000 examples, ordered and chaotic learning speed deteriorates markedly while critical accuracy deteriorates less. This qualitatively supports initialization-dependent learning speed.
relationships.display_finding: Critical initialization preserved the validation trajectory at 25,000 examples while ordered initialization slowed and lost accuracy; at 15,000 examples, critical accuracy deteriorated less while ordered and chaotic learning slowed markedly.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
